description: Receiving e-prescriptions, faxed and phoned-in prescriptions, and refill requests; DUR review; labels; counseling; about 14 prescriptions a business day
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patient safety (patients on chronic medications; allergies and medication history are only in the PMS); about $720 of receipts per business day; patients who are turned away fill elsewhere and may not return. The PMS vendor's stated RTO of 12 hours does not meet the 4-hour RTO; the paper downtime kit bridges the gap to the 24-hour MTD
manual_workaround: Paper downtime kit: weekly printed active-patient medication list, blank label stock and a handwritten label template, paper dispensing log entered after recovery; one-time 72-hour emergency refills when the prescriber cannot be reached (Fla. Stat. 465.0275(1)); send new acute prescriptions to a nearby pharmacy
dependent_third_parties: PMS vendor; e-prescribing network (through the PMS vendor); cloud fax vendor; internet service provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: Pharmacist-owner (only pharmacist on duty; the relief pharmacist is the only backup); the prescription department

description: EPCS intake and verification; Schedule II handling; controlled substance dispensing records; nightly PDMP report; electronic Schedule II orders with the CSOS certificate
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: PDMP report due by the close of the next business day (Fla. Stat. 893.055(3)(a)); EPCS records must be kept electronically and stay intact (21 CFR 1311.305); abrupt interruption of pain, seizure, or ADHD medication can harm patients; RPO set by the PMS vendor's backups
manual_workaround: No EPCS while the PMS is down. Schedule II only on a paper prescription or an emergency oral authorization followed by the prescriber's written prescription within 7 days (21 CFR 1306.11(d)); paper controlled substance log; check for duplicate electronic versions when the PMS returns (21 CFR 1311.200(g)); upload the PDMP report through the PDMP web portal or ask the department for an extension
dependent_third_parties: PMS vendor; e-prescribing network; Florida PDMP; drug wholesaler
dependent_people_or_facilities: Pharmacist-owner (only CSOS certificate holder and DEA registrant contact); locked controlled substance cabinet

description: Real-time claims to PBMs through the claims switch; copays; card payments; remittance reconciliation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 90% of prescriptions are paid by PBMs; claims can be submitted after recovery, but patients who cannot pay cash may go without; cash reserves cover about one month of drug purchases
manual_workaround: Dispense essential medications and hold claims for submission after recovery; offer cash pricing to those who prefer; record each held claim on the paper log; the card terminal runs on the processor's cellular connection and keeps working
dependent_third_parties: PMS vendor; claims switch (through the PMS vendor); PBMs; card processor

description: Master formulation records, compounding logs, beyond-use dating, and labels for about 40 compounded prescriptions a month
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Compounded prescriptions are usually planned a day or more ahead; records must be complete before release; version history in the file suite supports a 24-hour RPO
manual_workaround: Printed binder of master formulation records kept at the compounding bench; paper compounding logbook; delay non-urgent compounding
dependent_third_parties: Email and file suite vendor (no accepted BAA)

description: Refill reminder texts and the refill phone line (PMS features); email; ordering non-controlled stock from the wholesaler portal; accounting
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Daily wholesaler deliveries cover about 2 to 3 days of stock; reminders and email can wait; administrative deadlines are measured in days
manual_workaround: Phone calls from the store line; order by phone from the wholesaler; vendor web portals from the laptop
dependent_third_parties: Email and file suite vendor; drug wholesaler; accounting SaaS
